basics.name: Alex Mercer
basics.label: Principal Distributed Systems & AI Infrastructure Architect
basics.summary: Systems architect with 12+ years designing mission-critical distributed runtimes, low-latency agent orchestration frameworks, and autonomous developer tooling. Pioneer of deterministic multi-agent state machines and zero-dependency headless artifact pipelines.

work.name: Nexus Autonomous Systems
work.summary: Architected the core distributed execution engine powering 50,000+ concurrent autonomous coding agents across multi-cloud hybrid clusters.
highlights: Engineered sub-3ms task dispatch queue using Rust and io_uring, reducing p99 scheduling latency by 84%.
Designed isolated sandbox runtime with zero-copy memory telemetry and automated memory cap enforcement.
Authored the company-wide Technical Design Standards and piloted deterministic state recovery for long-running workflows.

work.name: Vortex Cloud Platform
work.summary: Led the global edge deployment team responsible for container orchestration, zero-trust traffic tunnels, and paged artifact compilation.
highlights: Built edge document compilation service delivering <50ms PDF synthesis for enterprise billing and reporting.
Scaled distributed edge ingress to 4.2M req/sec using eBPF-based traffic filtering and zero-trust mesh routing.
Mentored 14 senior engineers and spearheaded cross-functional incident postmortem processes.

work.name: Aether Data Labs
work.summary: Core contributor to real-time analytics streaming engine and columnar storage serialization formats.
highlights: Implemented high-throughput Apache Arrow columnar serializer achieving 12GB/s memory-to-disk throughput.
Refactored legacy clustering protocol to Raft consensus, eliminating split-brain edge cases.

projects.name: Turbine-FS
projects.description: High-performance userspace filesystem with content-addressed chunking and cryptographic deduplication.
highlights: Adopted by 12,000+ open-source developers; achieved 18GB/s read throughput in synthetic micro-benchmarks.
Written in 100% safe Rust with formal TLA+ verification for concurrent synchronization primitives.
